subject.title: Renderer placeholder leak: `(see attached image)`, `Image reply`, `Audio reply`, `Media reply` leak to human-visible Telegram reply under specific content-classification paths

question: Should the existing released-install report authorize implementation, or must a current-main Telegram payload trace first identify the exact placeholder-to-send boundary?
rationale: The issue is credible, but the inspected source does not establish which of several distinct placeholder representations reaches Telegram, and choosing the wrong owner could damage model prompt context.

options.title: Require payload trace
options.body: Capture a current-main Telegram run showing the placeholder in reply construction and the final Bot API text or caption before assigning a source fix.

options.title: Authorize source investigation
options.body: Allow an owner to instrument and repair the suspected boundary using the released reproduction as sufficient initial evidence.

recommendation.title: Require payload trace
recommendation.body: Capture a current-main Telegram run showing the placeholder in reply construction and the final Bot API text or caption before assigning a source fix.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work covers Telegram rendering behavior, and the issue timeline already routes this report to them.
